interface.title: WildlifeML – Wildlife Age-Sex Classification (Streamlit app)
interface.field: Wildlife ecology / camera-trap image analysis with machine learning
interface.stage_of_work: Labelling training data, then evaluating a trained classifier
interface.what_it_is_for: Label MegaDetector-detected animals in camera-trap images with user-defined age/sex classes, then review a trained classifier's metrics, confusion matrices, misclassified images and low-confidence predictions.

data.note: The 'demo' image directory has a saved annotation config (one class 'ex_class' with label_1 and label_2) and MegaDetector boxes in raw/md_unlabeled.json. Every box in it is already labelled. The model dropdown also lists many precomputed experiments besides demo_model (final_results/*, sex/*, age/*, tensorflow_archive/*). For those, metrics show, but the error and uncertainty slideshows report 'No model errors with valid images found' because their images are not on the server.

features.name: Evaluation dashboard with metric tiles and stratified breakdown
features.general: Choose a trained model from a list ranked by score, load its saved evaluation, read headline metrics and uncertainty counts, then see the same metrics per subgroup and per repeated run
features.specific: Select model (labelled with Avg Accuracy, best first) → View Results → Dataset Overview, Uncertainty Analysis (threshold, certain/uncertain counts, avg confidence), Overall Performance (accuracy, precision, recall, F1) → Stratified Results (e.g. is_summer True/False) → Individual Evaluation Runs expanders
steps: type in the Select model box to filter models and pick one
press View Results
read Overall Performance and Uncertainty Analysis tiles
scroll to Stratified Results to compare strata
expand an individual run to see its own metrics and strata

Rank candidate models by average accuracy before choosing one

features.name: Class-distribution treemap with drill-down, paired with confusion matrix

features.specific: 'Class Distribution & Confusion Matrix' expander: Plotly treemap of Aggregated Test Data (hover shows label/value; clicking a tile zooms into it, clicking the root header zooms back) above a matplotlib Aggregated Confusion Matrix

click the root header to zoom back out
read the confusion matrix below

features.name: Prediction review slideshow
features.general: Step through a filtered set of images one at a time, each with its ID, true label, predicted label and confidence, using first/previous/next/last controls and a progress bar
features.specific: Model Errors – Slideshow (Error Viewing) and Uncertain Images – Slideshow (Uncertainty Viewing): 'Image k of N', progress bar, image with Image ID caption, ⏮️ First / ⬅️ Previous / Next ➡️ / ⏭️ Last, True/Predicted Ex_Class and Confidence. The same pages also carry the per-run summary grid (f5) and the Training Specs card (f4).

view the current image with its true/predicted class and confidence
move with First/Previous/Next/Last

features.name: Training-spec card

features.specific: Training Specs expander (on Model Results and Uncertainty Viewing): Training Data Class Distribution treemap, Transfer Learning Phase and Fine-tuning Phase (epochs, patience, optimizer, learning rate, fine-tuned layers), Other Parameters (loss, batch size, early stop metric), Model Architecture code block with copy button

open_fixes: Labelling each detected box (box image, a picker per class, Previous / Save/Next / Skip, progress bar) needs a new run on a staged unlabelled collection, such as a copy of data/demo with empty annotations. Every demo box was already labelled, so no screen shows it.
Defining the label scheme with the 'Edit Class Definitions' table and 'Continue to annotation' needs a collection without annotation_config.json. Only 'demo' was offered and it already had a config.
The two matching features (box-labelling panel, class-definition editor) can only be added once that run reaches and cites those screens.

A real side-by-side comparison of models or experiments (e.g. age vs sex, experiment N vs M) was not explored beyond reading the ranked dropdown. It needs a run that opens and compares two or more models' results.
